basis: A lesion of peripheral nerves; no other organ involvement is intrinsic.
Congenital joint contractures and skeletal abnormalities with congenital heart defects or cardiomyopathy define the syndrome.
Intestinal schistosomiasis causes egg-mediated bowel inflammation; clinically damaging hepatic fibrosis is variable and not established in at least 30% across infections.
Congenital dysferlin-related skeletal myopathy; weakness and motor delay reflect muscle disease rather than primary nervous system damage.
Inherited immune dysregulation with hemophagocytosis and cytopenias; hepatic inflammation/dysfunction occurs in most and CNS inflammation in roughly 30-70% of familial HLH.

Inherited skeletal muscle hyperirritability with rippling contractions, mounding, stiffness and cramps.
Aortic sinus aneurysm and associated regurgitation are cardiovascular; stroke is very rare and dyspnea does not establish pulmonary damage.
A benign blood vessel neoplasm arising in and occupying the small intestine.
Hypogonadotropic hormone deficiency and frontoparietal hair loss jointly define the syndrome.
Autoinflammatory skin and bowel disease defines the syndrome; coarctation and hypertension in one reported patient do not establish common cardiovascular involvement.
Autoimmune inflammatory skeletal myopathy; overlap diseases are separately diagnosed, and cardiac damage is reported only in some patients.
Maternal riboflavin deficiency is a vitamin metabolism/transport disorder; neonatal consequences do not establish maternal organ damage.
The supplied definition describes bovine bacterial fibrinous bronchopneumonia, directly affecting the lungs.
Brachydactyly, cerebellar ataxia and persistent nystagmus form the defining skeletal, neurologic and ocular motor triad.
Colorectal adenomatous polyposis defines FAP; bone osteomas occur in 30-79% per HPO. CHRPE usually spares vision; thyroid nodules and cancers are separate diagnoses.
Inherited vesicoureteral reflux directly affects the urinary tract.
Classical Timothy syndrome without syndactyly features severe cardiac electrical dysfunction; neurodevelopmental impairment is common, roughly over 50%, though TS2 data are limited.
Osteopetrosis commonly obliterates marrow, causing cytopenias; optic disc pallor occurs in 11/12. Hepatomegaly is compensatory; primary neurodegeneration is subtype-dependent.
Carcinoma arising from esophageal glands; the esophagus is gastrointestinal.
Cleft palate, vertebral malformations and intellectual disability are defining features; external ear and facial morphology do not establish additional organ dysfunction.
An intracranial arterial aneurysm is vascular disease; brain injury after rupture is a potential complication rather than intrinsic established damage.
Familial hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with myocardial polyglucosan accumulation; no independent systemic metabolic disorder or extracardiac damage is established.
Migrating nematode larvae cause hepatic granulomatous inflammation; pneumonitis is common, approximately 40-60%. Reactive eosinophilia does not establish blood organ damage.
Defined by impaired ocular accommodation and focusing function.
